title: Parameter products define reduced Cartier divisors with dense complement
statement:
Let $Y$ be a locally Noetherian regular scheme [pqf-def-locnoeth, def-weil-regular-scheme] and let $t_1,\ldots,t_r\in\Gamma(Y,\mathcal O_Y)$, with $r\ge0$. Assume that for every $y\in Y$, in $B=\mathcal O_{Y,y}$ the sublist of nonunit germs $(t_j)_{j\in J_y}$, where $J_y=\{j:t_j\notin B^\times\}$, consists of members at distinct positions of a regular system of parameters [def-weil-pbc-regular-system-of-parameters]. Put $f=\prod_{i=1}^r t_i$, and let $H=V(f)\hookrightarrow Y$ be the closed subscheme cut out by the principal ideal sheaf $(f)$ [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Then $H$ is reduced [def-pc-reduced-scheme] and is an effective Cartier divisor [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal], and $D(f)=Y\setminus|H|$ is open dense in $Y$. More precisely, at every $y$, $B$ is a nonzero domain, each nonunit $t_j$ is prime, distinct such parameters do not divide one another, and
$$(f)B=\left(\prod_{j\in J_y}t_j\right)B=\bigcap_{j\in J_y}(t_j)B.$$
This ideal is radical and its generator is a non-zero-divisor. The empty intersection is $B$ and the empty product is $1$, so the conclusion includes empty $Y$ and empty $H$.

proof.text: Fix y and put B = O_{Y,y}. Regularity [def-weil-regular-scheme] and [lem-sc-regular-local-domain] give a nonzero domain. Apply clause (b) of [lem-sfb-transverse-prime-ideal-parameters] to the entire supplied parameter system (r = d). Its product is nonzero, hence every parameter is nonzero, and its principal prime ideals yield prime parameter elements via Ideal.span_singleton_prime. Its incomparability clause gives nondivisibility for the selected germs, since their positions are injective. For a finite family of pairwise nondividing primes, prove that the product ideal equals their intersection: induct on a finite set of indices; writing x = a_i b, primality and nondivisibility imply that all remaining primes divide b, and induction gives their product divides b. The reverse implication is factor divisibility. The intersection is radical by Ideal.isRadical_iInf. Split the full family into nonunit and unit subtypes with Fintype.prod_subtype_mul_prod_subtype; the second product is a unit, so Ideal.span_singleton_mul_right_unit identifies the full and selected product ideals. Every factor is a unit or one of the prime parameters, hence is nonzero; map_prod and prod_ne_zero_iff give a nonzero full germ product and thus its nonzerodivisor property. The finite-product argument includes the empty family without a dimension or nonemptiness restriction.

proof.text: For f the global product, put I = ofIdealTop(span {f}). At a point z of I.subscheme, choose an affine neighborhood U of its image. The existing proved Scheme.Hom.ker_stalkMap from WeilConjectures.Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.Morphisms.ClosedImmersion identifies the kernel of the surjective stalk map of this closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] with the extension of I(U). Rewrite with ker_subschemeι, ofIdealTop_ideal, Ideal.map_span, and germ_res_apply: the kernel is exactly span {f_y}. It is radical by step 1. Mathlib RingHom.ker_isRadical_iff_reduced_of_surjective gives reducedness of the target stalk. Apply isReduced_of_isReduced_stalk [def-pc-reduced-scheme] to obtain reducedness of the closed subscheme. This uses the existing stalk-kernel API directly rather than reconstructing the quotient-localization isomorphism.

Let I = ofIdealTop(span {f}). Its subscheme inclusion has kernel I by ker_subschemeι. At every y choose an affine neighborhood U. Rewrite ofIdealTop_ideal, Ideal.map_span and germ_res_apply to identify the extension of its ideal with span {f_y}. Step 1 gives f_y in nonZeroDivisors; applying this to the difference of two elements gives injectivity of multiplication by f_y. The scheme clause isInvertible_ker_of_stalk_nonzerodivisor of [lem-sfb-stalk-nonzerodivisor-cartier-spreading], using local Noetherianity from hY, proves that I is an effective Cartier ideal [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal]. The generator is allowed to be a unit and the argument is vacuous on an empty scheme.

Apply [lem-pc-cartier-divisor-nowhere-dense] to the invertibility just proved and take its topological-density clause. The identities coe_support_ofIdealTop, zeroLocus_span and zeroLocus_singleton identify the complement of the support with the basic open of f. This proves density. Empty Y and an empty factor family are included by the existing complement theorem and the finite-product conventions.
